clue.text: Somewhere in Kent with unusual farm building

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the word before it are put into a new, unfamiliar order

parts.note: a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: A Kent location boasts an odd barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges WITH into WHIT. Whitstable is a seaside town on the north Kent coast, famous for oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is an example of a place in the county of Kent, so the vague phrase stands for it.

clue.text: Report of one-time occupant of Reading gaol being unruly

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the name that follows is said aloud and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was imprisoned in Reading Gaol and wrote a ballad about it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a former prisoner of Reading gaol as badly behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town west of London; its prison held the writer Oscar Wilde in the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unruly children are uncontrolled and boisterous, out of hand.

clue.text: Pauses in school period — sit sloppily

parts.note: taken as written
a term is one division of the school year

indicators.note: sloppily says the letters of the word beside it are put together carelessly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Breaks occur during term when someone slouches in their chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppily' is the anagram signal for the last word; the first 'in' is part of the answer, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is a formal verb meaning to suspend or stop for a time, so it means pauses.

clue.text: Horse in street starts to exasperate every driver

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A horse in the road annoys every motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a steed is a literary word for a horse, especially one ridden.

clue.text: Attend to a daughter wanting party attire, say?

parts.note: a dress is an example of what might be worn to a party; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A girl with nothing to wear to a party, and a parent who must deal with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to address a problem is to deal with it or turn your attention to it.

clue.text: Land with little hesitation, carrying less weight

parts.note: to light on something is to land or settle on it, as a bird does
er is the small sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A pilot touches down after a brief pause, the aircraft now unburdened.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative adjective: something weighing less than another is the less heavy of the two.

clue.text: Greeting given by Matthew etc bringing a suggestion

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
Matthew and the other gospels are books of the New Testament, abbreviated NT

explanation.surface: A greeting from Matthew and friends carries a gentle prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hint is an indirect suggestion or clue.

clue.text: Home rented out — bit of a lake here?

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a let property is one rented out to tenants

explanation.surface: A lakeside cottage is rented to holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of water running into the shore, so part of a lake might be one; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Model Major-General?

parts.note: plays on the Gilbert and Sullivan song 'the very model of a modern Major-General': a model, or miniature, of an army officer is a plaything figure

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls the patter song in The Pirates of Penzance; 'model' is read as a miniature rather than an ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small figure of an army officer, made as a child's plaything, is a model of a Major-General.

clue.text: Drink overdue — time to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the time letter goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: late means overdue

explanation.surface: A coffee order is running late, and the clock steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a milky coffee, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Using fingers or employing electronic equipment?

definitions.meaning: digits are fingers, so doing something with them is done by digit
digital devices work in numbers, so anything done by computer is done this way

explanation.definitionFit: Digit means both finger and numeral, so the adverb covers handwork and computer work.

clue.text: Fault limited by your being frugal

indicators.note: limited by means held within bounds, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
a rift is a fault or crack, as in rock

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for being stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone frugal is careful with money and avoids waste.

clue.text: Embarrassed maiden has to consume non-vegetarian food

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
M stands for maiden, a cricket over with no runs
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A blushing girl is made to eat a steak.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden over is one with no runs scored; scorecards write it M.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and lamb are examples of meat, which a vegetarian avoids.

clue.text: Fashion of yesteryear conveyed by Margaret Rose

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Princess Margaret Rose models old-fashioned clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates the look of earlier decades.

clue.text: King, by Jove, going round that place to be met again

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: going round says one word wraps around another

parts.note: egad and by Jove are both old mild oaths
there means that place

explanation.surface: A monarch exclaims as he circles a spot for a reunion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps the oath around the place word, which goes in before its final letter, giving EGATHERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be regathered is to be brought together once more, so it means assembled again.

clue.text: Problems unchanged about drink being knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the whole assembled string is read in reverse
about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: same means unchanged
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Trouble persists after someone downs a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses the whole container, SAMGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: enigmas are puzzles or mysteries that are hard to solve.

clue.text: Chap dined on Eastern sea creature

parts.note: a chap is a man
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A man ate an Asian sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea cow is a large aquatic mammal, an example of a marine creature.

clue.text: Faulty electric plug may have to be thus rejected

definitions.text: Faulty electric plug may have to be thus
definitions.meaning: a British plug holds a fuse; a faulty one may need its fuse replaced, being given a fuse again

explanation.walkthrough: British mains plugs each contain a small cartridge fuse that is replaced when it blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two parts, the word means fitted with a fuse again; read whole, it means turned down.

clue.text: Her cat's OK, having got crumbled biscuit

indicators.note: crumbled means broken into pieces, so the letters of the words before are reassembled

explanation.surface: The cat is fine after eating a broken biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' sits beside 'biscuit' but signals the rearrangement of HERCATSOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a crumbly, buttery biscuit, an example of the type.

clue.text: Idiot, dispatched to be locked up, agrees

indicators.note: locked up means imprisoned, held inside, so this word goes inside the first

parts.note: an ass is a fool
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A fool, sent off to jail, goes along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who assents agrees or gives consent.

clue.text: A diner's stewed fish

indicators.note: stewed means mixed up as in a pot, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer's cooked fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard family member is a small oily fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Feature of seasonal dance, mum meeting unknown European

parts.note: ma is a name for mother, mum
Y is an algebra unknown
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Mother meets a foreigner at a spring dance.
explanation.walkthrough: May Day celebrations in Britain feature dancing round a ribboned pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall ribboned pole is the centrepiece of the traditional May Day dance.

clue.text: Ideal partner with strength to restrict bishop

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine, so the bishop goes inside the word for strength

parts.note: might means strength
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A strong partner is held back by a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the perfect man someone hopes to marry.

clue.text: Get lost in hole at back of house

indicators.note: at back of says this piece follows the next one in the answer

parts.note: a pit is a hole

explanation.surface: Someone told to go away ends up in a hole behind the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive British commands telling someone to leave: go away.

clue.text: Nutty type in church in little sleep, having rolled over

indicators.note: rolled over means turned upside down, so the assembled letters read upwards in this down answer
in says the church abbreviation is placed within the sleep

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An eccentric dozes off in church and turns over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having rolled over' reverses NACEP. 'Nutty type' looks like a crank but means a kind of nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is a kind of nut, so it is a nutty type in a literal sense.

clue.text: Two groups of soldiers nibbled Welsh food?

parts.note: the Royal Artillery is RA
the Royal Engineers are RE
bit means nibbled

explanation.surface: Two army units munched on something in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rabbit or rarebit is melted cheese on toast; the question mark covers dropping 'Welsh' from the dish's name.

clue.text: Female at match to bristle, getting left out

indicators.note: out signals the letter for left is removed from the word

parts.note: to bridle is to bristle with anger or resentment

explanation.surface: A woman at a football game gets angry and walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like sport but means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage, and the woman getting married at it is its central female figure.

clue.text: Military building supporting regiment finally

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: finally says take the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A stronghold backing the regiment at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort is a fortified military stronghold.

clue.text: Get cork in — when loosened it could be this!

definitions.text: Get cork in — when loosened it could be this!

indicators.note: loosened means freed up, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Push a cork into a bottle; when it comes free it flies off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when loosened' rearranges GETCORKIN, and a cork freed from a champagne bottle shoots upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketing means shooting up fast, as a champagne cork does when released.

clue.text: This person's past appearing in ideal representation

parts.note: the setter's 'this person is' becomes I'M
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone's history shows up in a perfect image of them.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis an imago is an idealised mental image of a person, often a parent.

clue.text: Stupid person about to get lost in mound of sand

indicators.note: to get lost means to disappear, so the letter for about is dropped

parts.note: a dunce is a stupid person
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A fool is about to lose their way among sand hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A dune is a hill of sand piled up by wind.

clue.text: Subsidence in local community

definitions.meaning: the gradual sinking of ground or a building
a small village or group of homes where people have settled

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a building's sinking into the ground and a place where people have come to live.
